extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers and practitioners working on satire/irony/sarcasm detection, dataset creators, and computational linguistics scholars
extracted.subtask_description: Creation and evaluation of a sentence-level dataset for detecting satire in Romanian news articles; includes manual annotations and baseline model evaluations (LLMs and transformers) in zero-shot and fine-tuning settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence-level granularity
rubrics_metrics.description: First sentence-level dataset for Romanian satire detection for news articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors emphasize sentence-level annotation because "satirical information [can be] incorporated into news articles" at a more granular level than article-level labels. The dataset is explicitly designed at sentence granularity to support this finer-grained task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual annotation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract states the dataset "comprises 13,873 manually annotated sentences," indicating human labels are used rather than distant or weak supervision; manual annotation is presented as a quality criterion for the dataset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain diversity / topical coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentences span various domains including social issues, IT, science, and movies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dataset covers multiple topical domains (listed as "social issues, IT, science, and movies"), which the authors present as important for robustness and generality of satire-detection models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset size / scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Total of 13,873 annotated sentences in the dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The concrete size (13,873 sentences) is provided as a dataset characteristic that affects training and evaluation choices for models; scale is presented as part of dataset quality and utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline evaluation protocols (LLMs and transformers; zero-shot and fine-tuning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation uses multiple baseline models based on large language models (LLMs) in both zero-shot and fine-tuning settings, as well as baseline transformer-based models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper evaluates models in zero-shot and fine-tuning setups and compares LLM-based approaches with transformer baselines. This establishes recommended evaluation protocols and highlights which experimental settings are relevant for the task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting limitations and directions for future work
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical findings should report current limitations of models on sentence-level satire detection and suggest new research directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract notes that their "findings reveal the current limitations of these models in the sentence-level satire detection task, paving the way for new research directions," implying that dataset papers should include analysis of failure modes and guidance for future research.
